skill.name: pricing-contrast-set
skill.description: Design the three-tier contrast-set architecture — decoy / target / anchor. Applies asymmetric dominance (Ariely) so the decoy makes the target obviously better, the anchor sets the high reference frame, and ~75% of buyers land on the target tier. Loaded by the main pricing skill when the operator asks to design tiers, redesign the pricing page, or apply the decoy effect. Outputs tier definitions, feature differentiation, value-metric scaling per tier, and the predicted landing distribution.
skill.summary: Design three pricing tiers with a shared value metric, differentiated features, buyer profiles, and testable adoption estimates.
skill.author: cmj-hub

remediation.suggestion: Use a recommendation label for untested tiers. Reserve popularity claims for verified sales data and distinguish adoption estimates from measured results.

semantic_findings.title: Unsupported Popularity Claim in Pricing Copy
semantic_findings.description: The skill requests ready-to-ship copy with the target tier labeled "Most Popular" and repeats that label in its output template. It uses predicted adoption without requiring observed sales, creating a risk of misleading buyers through unsupported social proof.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow and output template explicitly prescribe a popularity label without a supporting-data condition. Some operators may have supporting data, but the instructions do not require it.

content.value_statement: Unclear pricing tiers make product comparisons difficult and obscure the preferred offer. This skill structures three tiers with comparable quantities, distinct features, and testable adoption estimates.
actual_capabilities: Review current tier adoption against the framework's diagnostic thresholds.
Define decoy, target, and anchor tiers using a shared value metric.
Specify tier prices, quantities, features, buyer profiles, and predicted adoption shares.
Check quantity discounts, anchor credibility, feature clarity, and annual prepayment rules.
Draft pricing-card copy and identify where anchor copy should appear.
Recommend a pricing experiment and hand off test design to a companion skill.
limitations: Adoption percentages and performance claims are framework assumptions, not validated forecasts or guaranteed results.
The reviewed package contains one instruction file; referenced documentation and companion skills are not included.
It drafts recommendations and copy but does not deploy pages, run experiments, or measure outcomes.
Its rules target B2B SaaS and services; other markets and customer needs may require different tier structures.

use_cases.title: Create Initial SaaS Tiers
use_cases.description: Define three plans with comparable seat quantities, feature differences, prices, and intended buyers before testing demand.

use_cases.title: Diagnose an Existing Pricing Structure
use_cases.description: Use recent tier adoption data to identify unclear differentiation and propose a revised comparison.

use_cases.title: Draft Pricing-Page Cards
use_cases.description: Turn approved tiers into concise comparison copy and prepare recommendations for a pricing experiment.

prompt_templates.title: Outline Three Tiers
prompt_templates.prompt: Design three pricing tiers for [product] using [value metric]. Include quantities, prices, features, and intended buyers. State assumptions and missing inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create an initial tier proposal.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Tier Adoption
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [current tiers] and [90-day adoption shares]. Diagnose tier differentiation using this framework. Separate observed data from assumptions and recommend changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess existing plans using supplied data.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Pricing Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft pricing cards for [approved tiers]. Keep one shared value metric and concise feature lists. Use popularity claims only when [sales evidence] supports them.

prompt_templates.title: Develop a Testable Redesign
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign [tier structure] using [buyer profiles], [target contract value], and [adoption history]. Explain tradeoffs, label forecasts, and prepare a companion-skill test-design handoff.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: connect tier strategy with experiment planning.

output_examples.input: Propose seat-based plans for a collaboration tool with a $300 monthly target plan and a real larger-team buyer.
output: Starter: $90 monthly for 5 seats, with core collaboration.
Team: $300 monthly for 25 seats, with core collaboration and audit logs.
Scale: $900 monthly for 100 seats, with all Team features, SSO, and priority support.
Per-seat costs decrease from $18 to $12 to $9. Validate prices and adoption assumptions before launch.

output_examples.input: Our last 90 days show 30% Starter, 45% Team, and 25% Scale adoption. What should we review?
output: Starter adoption exceeds the framework's 20% diagnostic threshold.
Team adoption falls below its 50% target-tier diagnostic threshold.
Review Team pricing, feature clarity, and whether Starter serves a legitimate customer segment.
Treat these thresholds as hypotheses. Test changes before replacing the existing plans.

best_practices: Supply current tiers, a shared value metric, buyer profiles, and recent adoption data.
Keep every tier credible and use verified evidence for popularity labels.
Label adoption forecasts as hypotheses and validate the redesign through controlled testing.
anti_patterns: Comparing tiers with incompatible value metrics or unclear feature differences.
Creating a fictional premium tier only to make another plan appear inexpensive.
Publishing predicted adoption as measured demand or guaranteeing the framework's performance claims.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces tier definitions, prices, quantities, feature differences, buyer profiles, adoption estimates, and pricing-card copy.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide current tiers, the shared value metric, buyer profiles, and recent adoption shares. The workflow expects these inputs from business configuration.

faq.question: Does it guarantee that most buyers choose the target tier?
faq.answer: No. Its target adoption range is a framework assumption. Actual demand requires measurement and testing.

faq.question: Are the companion skills included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains only SKILL.md. Anchor-copy references and experiment-design skills must be available separately.

faq.question: Can it publish a page or run an A/B test?
faq.answer: No. It drafts pricing copy and recommends a handoff for test design. It does not provide deployment or experiment execution tools.

faq.question: When can I label a tier Most Popular?
faq.answer: Use that label only when verified purchase data supports it. For untested tiers, use a recommendation label without claiming observed popularity.
